newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher across the board.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher across the board on Sunday with strong demand for unlinked bonds from the mutual funds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.18 pct to 105.89
Volume including Makams was 192 million shekels.

"There was strong demand for unlinked bonds especially Makams because mutual funds specialising in unlinked bonds buy them at the beginning of each month," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.
But demand was up across the board because of expectations for lower interest rates in coming months, he said.

"The market is in a holding pattern, with players buying all kinds of bonds because they expect the central bank to continue to lower interest rates, if not next month then the month after. Inflation in the coming months is also expected to be lower, with forecasts of nine percent for the coming 12 months," Halpern said.

"Trading today was calm. The market is concentrating mainly on equities. Activity in the bond market is mainly in the unlinked bonds, because of expectations of lower inflation in the coming months. CPI-linked bonds are generally less interesting in the summer months (when inflation is seasonally lower)," said Danny Alt, portfolio manager at Nesuah Trading and Investment.
Trading in dollar-linked bonds was stable, he added.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
